newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-HINGIS BEATS NOVOTNA TO ADVANCE TO FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HINGIS BEATS NOVOTNA TO ADVANCE TO FINAL.

text.p: Martina Hingis used her only ace of the match to seal a hard-fought victory over Jana Novotna Thursday that kept her win streak alive and lifted her to the final of the $4.45 million Lipton Championships.
Fighting through sizzling temperatures, the top-seeded Hingis defeated third seed Novotna 6-3 2-6 6-4 for her 25th consecutive match victory.
The 16-year-old Swiss, already assured of becoming the youngest player to reach the number one ranking, has appeared in four finals this year, winning them all.
Hingis will play the winner of Thursday's later semifinal between fourth-seeded American Monica Seles and 11th seed Barbara Paulus of Austria.
"It was a good match," said Hingis. "We both played a very high standard. She makes you run and make a lot of mistakes you shouldn't and that you don't do against other players."

Hingis appeared to have the match in control early, breaking Novotna for a 2-0 lead and varying her shots to keep the net-rushing Czech off balance. She won the first set 6-3 with a blistering backhand up the line.
Novotna got the first break in the second set to lead 3-1 and held onto the advantage, breaking Hingis again to take the set 6-2 with a forehand winner.
After that, both players left the court for the optional 10-minute break allowed under the rules during hot weather. It was Hingis who came back more refreshed.

Hingis fought off break points in the eighth game with well placed passing shots, then broke a weary Novotna for 5-4 as the Czech double-faulted, then dumped an easy forehand into the net. Hingis served out the match with her first ace, 6-4.
"She is a very unpredictable kind of player," said Novotna. "The thing I would change today would be my return of serve but otherwise I thought I played really well."
Hingis said the fitter player won the match. "I felt pretty good still in the third set and the break helped a lot. The conditions meant the player who was fittest would win."
